full_judgment:
The present respondent No. 2 as plaintiff originally filed a suit being Artha Rin Suit No. 341 of 2020 before respondent No. 1 claiming an amount of Taka 25,11,336/62 against the present respondent No. 3 and another as defendant Nos. 1-2 stating inter alia that, the respondent No. 3 availed a cash credit facilities amounting to Taka 15,08,450/93 and that of the term loan of Taka 10,02,885/69 totaling Taka 25,11,336/62 from respondent No. 2. As the said defendant failed to repay the loan as per the terms and .conditions set out in the sanctioned letter, the respondent No. 2 filed the suit. In course of the suit, this petitioner on 10-4-2021 filed an application under order 1, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for impleading him as party to the suit contending inter alia that, he purchased 1.50 kathas of land from the defendant No. 1 named, Md Jahirul Islam (respondent No. 3 herein) and accordingly, he mutated his name in the khatian and has been paying rent since the purchase and started residing therein by erecting homestead upon taking connection of the utilities without any interruption from any quarters. Afterwards, the petitioner came to learn that the said defendant, Md Jahirul Islam by mortgaging the said property took loan from respondent No. 2 by executing and registering a mortgage deed in its favour on 31-5-2016 and also registered a power of attorney in favour of the said respondent No. 2. Having learned, the petitioner then filed the application. Against the said application, the respondent No. 2 filed a written objection denying all the materials allegations made in the petition for addition of party. However, the learned Judge took up the said application for hearing on 9-9-2021 and rejected the application reasoning that, there has been no scope to implead any person as party to a Artha Rin Suit other than the persons so provided in section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and on that sole ground, the said application of the petitioner was rejected. 

 11. The case in hand, we find that, this petitioner had admittedly purchased the property prior to mortgaging the same to the respondent No. 2 by the respondent No. 3 and it has clearly been asserted in the application that, soon after purchasing the same, he (petitioner) mutated his name in the Khatian and erected one-storied building and also planted different types of trees by mutating his name in the khatian and has been paying khazna to the respective Tahshil Office. So by that, he acquired an indefeasible right and title over the said property and thereby his presence is very much required in disposing of the suit effectively. We thus find that, the petitioner is a proper and necessary party in whose presence the suit should be disposed of. In view of the above, we are inclined to make the Rule absolute.
